title: Rabbi Binyamin bar Yefet
author: Aharon Hyman
attribution: Model-assisted translation, editorially reviewed; publication authorized by Joshua Waxman.

paragraphs: He was Rabbi Yochanan’s student, as in Berakhot 38b: Rabbi Zeira wondered at it: “What has Rabbi Binyamin bar Yefet to do with Rabbi Chiyya bar Abba? … Rabbi Binyamin bar Yefet was not precise; he did not review.” Hyman infers from this that he was Rabbi Yochanan’s student, although not a distinguished student like Rabbi Chiyya bar Abba.

In Shabbat 53a and Ketubot 77a: when Rabbi Zeira went up, he found Rabbi Binyamin bar Yefet sitting and saying in Rabbi Yochanan’s name. Likewise “Rabbi Binyamin bar Yefet said that Rabbi Yochanan said,” as in Pesachim 54a, Jerusalem Talmud Pesachim 2:5 and Tanchuma, Lekh Lekha 10; Bereshit Rabbah 43:3 reads “in the name of Rabbi Yonatan,” and Hyman proposes Rabbi Yochanan. In Berakhot 33a: “Rabbi Binyamin bar Yefet said: Rabbi Yose [son of Rabbi Chanina] asked Rabbi Yochanan in Sidon.”

Likewise “Rabbi Binyamin bar Yefet said that Rabbi Elazar said,” as in Taanit 29b, Yoma 29a, Megillah 16b, Sanhedrin 7a, Shevuot 18b and Chullin 50b and 52b according to the Rosh’s reading. In Jerusalem Talmud Sanhedrin 1:1: Rabbi Ba and Rabbi Binyamin bar Yefet had a lawsuit and came to Rabbi Yitzchak, who ruled in favor of Rabbi Binyamin bar Yefet.

notes.text: Saved Davidson Taanit29b fully writes Rabbi Elazar for the cited Binyamin teaching. This supports the contextual expansion instead of a mechanical resh-aleph rule. Pesachim2:5 is Jerusalem Talmud, and the Yose/Yonatan/Assi corrections remain Hyman’s. The supplied לא דיין is read in the precise-reviewing sense indicated by the adjoining לא מהדר.

The inspected Berakhot 38b directly contrasts Chiyya bar Abba’s precision and repeated study with Binyamin bar Yefet’s report in Yochanan’s name. This is the basis of Hyman’s student-status inference, not a new authority relation. His Yonatan-to-Yochanan proposal, bracketed Yose patronymic and exact Rosh readings remain occurrence-specific and attributed.
